documents.title: Top 21 Things To Do In Varanasi (2026 Edition) - Varanasi Guru
documents.content:
A thoughtfully curated guide to India’s spiritual and cultural capital
Introduction
Varanasi, also known as Kashi or Benares, is not just a destination – it’s an experience. Believed to be one of the world’s oldest living cities, Varanasi pulses with devotion, history, art, and raw human emotion. From serene boat rides on the Ganges to walking through ancient alleys echoing with chants, the city invites you to slow down, look deeper, and feel more.
If you’re planning a visit, here are 21 meaningful things to do in Varanasi that capture its essence.
Table of Contents
1. Attend the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat
An iconic evening ritual where priests offer fire to the river with synchronized movements, mantras, and music. Arrive early to find a good spot, or view it from a boat for a more serene perspective.
2. Begin Your Day with Subah-e-Banaras at Assi Ghat
A unique morning experience that blends live classical music, yoga, and spiritual chants. It’s the city’s quiet soul before the rush begins.
3. Take a Sunrise Boat Ride on the Ganges
The best way to see the ghats and temples lining the river while the city slowly wakes up. This is also the golden hour for photography.
4. Visit the Kashi Vishwanath Temple
Dedicated to Lord Shiva, this is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and a deeply revered site. Note that security is tight, and photography is not allowed inside the temple complex.
5. Witness Cremations at Manikarnika Ghat
This sacred cremation ground operates day and night. Though intense, it offers a profound look at the cycle of life and the belief in moksha (liberation).
6. Explore Ramnagar Fort
A former royal residence on the eastern bank of the Ganges. It houses a museum with vintage cars, costumes, and artifacts, along with sweeping views of the river.
7. Walk Through Varanasi’s Ancient Alleys
The narrow streets around Vishwanath Gali are filled with surprises – hidden shrines, age-old shops, local crafts, and the scent of incense and marigolds.
8. Enjoy a Traditional Banarasi Breakfast
Start your morning with kachori-sabzi, jalebi, and chai served in clay cups. During winter, try the seasonal delicacy malaiyyo – a saffron-infused milk froth.
9. Shop for Banarasi Sarees and Handlooms
Visit local weavers or government emporiums to witness the intricate artistry behind Varanasi’s famous silk sarees.
10. Visit the Leaning Temple (Ratneshwar Mahadev)
Near Manikarnika Ghat, this submerged temple leans dramatically, making it one of the city’s most intriguing sights.
11. Explore Panchganga Ghat
Said to be the meeting point of five sacred rivers, this ghat holds historic importance and was the original site of Dev Diwali celebrations.
12. Take a Day Trip to Sarnath
Located just 10 km away, this is where Buddha gave his first sermon. Visit the Dhamek Stupa, Ashoka Pillar, and serene monasteries from different Buddhist traditions.
13. Visit the Home of Bismillah Khan
The late shehnai maestro’s home still resonates with musical legacy. A visit here, if arranged with local contacts, gives insight into Banaras’s musical heritage.
14. Practice Yoga by the Ganges
Many ghats and rooftop spaces offer yoga sessions. The tranquil setting enhances the meditative experience.
15. Sample Local Street Food
Try tamatar chaat, baati chokha, litti, and thandai. Walkable food tours can help you discover clean and authentic vendors.
16. Watch a Wrestling Session at a Traditional Akhara
Pehlwans still train in mud pits using age-old techniques. A guide can take you to one of these akharas where tradition thrives.
17. Attend a Classical Music or Dance Performance
Varanasi is a cradle of Indian classical arts. Keep an eye out for intimate performances in cultural centers or ashrams.
18. Visit Bharat Kala Bhavan Museum at BHU
A well-curated museum with rare textiles, sculptures, paintings, and artefacts reflecting India’s artistic legacy.
19. Offer a Lamp During Deep Daan
Participate in the quiet ritual of placing earthen lamps in the Ganges at dusk—a spiritual moment open to all visitors.
20. Explore the Home of Bhartendu Harishchandra
Known as the father of modern Hindi literature, his residence in Varanasi offers a literary dimension to the city’s heritage.
21. Join a Guided Heritage Walk
The best way to understand Varanasi’s layers is with a knowledgeable storyteller who can take you beyond the obvious into the city’s forgotten corners and secret courtyards.

documents.title: Top 5 Must-Do Scenic Boat Rides In Varanasi - Varanasi Guru
documents.author: Varanasi Guru
documents.content:
Varanasi, one of the oldest cities in the world, offers some of the most captivating boat rides along the holy Ganges River. From peaceful sunrise moments to mesmerizing Ganga Aarti views, these boat rides provide a unique perspective of the city’s spiritual and cultural essence. If you’re planning a visit, here are the top 5 boat rides in Varanasi that you can’t miss.
1. Subah-e-Banaras Morning Boat Ride
Start your day in Varanasi with the magical Subah-e-Banaras boat ride. The serene early morning hours provide the perfect backdrop to witness the river’s gentle flow while the city slowly comes to life. The sunrise over the ghats, coupled with the peaceful ambiance, offers a truly spiritual experience. Whether you’re an early riser or simply seeking a peaceful escape, this boat ride in Varanasi is a must-do for those looking to connect with the city’s soul.
- Key Highlights: Sunrise views, rituals on ghats, early morning tranquility
2. Evening Boat Ride with Ganga Aarti
A sunset boat ride in Varanasi is one of the most iconic experiences you can have. The boat will take you to Dashashwamedh Ghat, where you can witness the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti ceremony. The sight of hundreds of lamps lighting up the Ganges in the evening is truly magical. If you’re visiting during the evening, don’t miss the Ganga Aarti varanasi from boat for an unforgettable spiritual experience.
- Key Highlights: Ganga Aarti, vibrant sunset views, spiritual rituals
- Keywords: ganga aarti varanasi from boat, varanasi boat ride booking, boat tour varanasi
3. 51 Ghats, Kashi Darshan Boat Ride
For those looking to explore the full breadth of Varanasi’s ghats, the Kashi Darshan boat ride is a perfect choice. This boat ride takes you across all 51 ghats, offering a comprehensive view of the city’s temples, rituals, and everyday life along the riverbanks. A boat tour in Varanasi like this is an excellent way to learn about the history and significance of the city’s sacred spaces.
- Key Highlights: All 51 ghats, temples, historical insights
4. All Ghats Boat Ride
The All Ghats boat ride is a fantastic way to see the major ghats of Varanasi at a relaxed pace. From the bustling Dashashwamedh Ghat to the quieter Assi Ghat, this boat ride takes you on a journey through the heart of Varanasi. The calm waters of the Ganges offer a peaceful way to witness the city’s rich spiritual heritage, making this boat ride a must for any visitor.
- Key Highlights: Dashashwamedh Ghat, Assi Ghat, peaceful exploration
5. Mehfil-e-Banaras All Ghats Boat Ride with Storyteller
For a truly immersive experience, opt for the Mehfil-e-Banaras all ghats boat ride, which comes with a knowledgeable storyteller. As you float past the ghats, the storyteller will narrate fascinating stories, legends, and historical facts about Varanasi, adding depth to your journey. This boat ride in Varanasi offers a unique combination of cultural exploration and scenic beauty, providing a rich and educational experience.
- Key Highlights: Narrated stories, cultural insights, all ghats exploration
Whether you’re in search of spiritual enlightenment, breathtaking views, or cultural immersion, boating in Varanasi offers something for every traveler. From the tranquil morning boat rides to the spectacular Ganga Aarti experience from a boat, these journeys will leave you with unforgettable memories. If you’re unable to book one of the suggested times, don’t worry – you can take a boat ride at any time of the day to soak in the mesmerizing views of the ghats and the serene beauty of the Ganges. Each moment on the water in Varanasi is a unique experience waiting to be cherished.
Book your Varanasi boat ride in advance to make the most of your visit!

documents.title: Trailanga Swami: The Walking Shiv Of Kashi!
documents.author: Saurabh Rastogi
documents.content:
Kashi is a land of spiritual mysticism and ancient traditions, where countless saints and yogis have left an indelible mark on the country’s spiritual landscape. Among these luminaries, Trailanga Swami stands out as an extraordinary figure renowned for his incredible miracles and unwavering devotion. Today we will delve into the life and miracles of Trailanga Swami, a yogi who achieved legendary status for his remarkable abilities and deep spiritual insights.
The Life of Trailanga Swami
Trailanga Swami, also known as Shri Krishnendra swami or Swamiji Maharaj, was born in 1607 in the Kumbilapuram of Vizianagaram in Andhra Pradesh, India. From a young age, he exhibited an intense inclination towards spirituality and, by his teens, was drawn to the ascetic path. Trailanga Swami served his parents and after the death of his father, he gave all his wealth to the younger brother, he served his mother until her death when he was 52 years old.
After the death of his mother, Trailanga Swami spent 20 years practising meditation and yoga at a cremation ground wearing the ashes of his mother until he met his guru Swami Bhagirathananda Saraswati in 1679. Bhagirathanada guided Trailanga swami and helped him in taking the monastic vows and renaming him Swami Ganapati Saraswati in 1685.
Swami Ganapati spent most of his time travelling to various places before settling in Varanasi in 1737 where he lived in many places like Assi Ghat, Hanuman Ghat, Dashaswamedh Ghat, Panchganga Ghat etc.
Miracles of Trailanga Swami
While there is a long list of miracles related to Trailanga Swami, we will only speak of the ones that are well-documented in Varanasi.
One widely documented incident from Trailanga Swami’s life is from the British era. Trailanga Swami was not fond of materials and was often seen roaming around naked at the ghats. The Britishers didn’t like it and imprisoned him at the Chowk Thana police station for indecency. However, one day, as the guards were performing their routine checks, they discovered that the cell was empty. There was no sign of forced escape or any breach in the prison walls. It seemed as if Trailanga Swami had simply vanished into thin air and later on he was seen walking naked on the roof of the police station. He was again imprisoned but he disappeared from the jail the same night. The baffled jail authorities could not explain his disappearance.
Trailanga Swami could go without food or water for extended periods. His body seemed to operate on a different plane, not bound by the usual requirements of sustenance. On many days he only consumed milk and curd that was offered by his devotees and yet he never appeared straving. On other days he was just seen floating on the Ganga or sitting on hot sand under the harsh sun.
It is believed that Trailanga Swami lived for 280 years and that is why sometimes he is denoted as the immortal yogi. His interactions with people span multiple generations and centuries.
Death/Maha Samadhi of Trailanga Swami
Trailanga Swami was well aware of his death and he also informed his disciples that they would have to come in 5-6 years once invited without any fail.
When the time came he sent invites to his disciples and Instruct them in minute detail about his departure, he had them construct a wooden box precisely to his size. He directed them to place his body in the box without cremation. He specified the route, a rented boat journey from Assighat to Varunaghat where the box was to be submerged in the Ganges, at a specific spot a little distance from Panchganga Ghat.
Before his departure, he addressed his disciples’ spiritual questions, assigning the spiritual welfare of Umacharan to his second disciple, Kalicharan. News of Sri Trailanga Swami’s departure created a stir in Kashi. On the designated day, he retired into his room and entered a trance, emerging later to sit in a yoga posture in the wooden box, departing from his earthly existence at the age of 280 on December 26, 1887.
Shree Trailanga Swami Math
The Trailanga Swami Math stands proudly near Panchganga Ghat, right beside the Alamgir Mosque. Within its sacred walls, a divine Kali Murti revered by Trailanga Swami himself is enshrined. Near to this idol rests an immense Shivling, legend has it, brought by the Swami from the riverbed of the holy Ganges.
A remarkable statue of Trailanga Swami, commissioned by his devoted disciples at his behest, graces the temple. Beneath this statue lies an underground meditation chamber where the Swami spent countless hours in deep meditation. It was here, within the tranquillity of this sanctum, that Trailanga Swami drew his final breath, departing from this earthly realm.
Trailanga Swami’s life in Varanasi was truly mystical. His disappearing acts and ability to live without food are still fascinating stories that hold a lot of wonder.
His departure, meticulously orchestrated, mirrored the depth of his teachings, marking the end of an earthly chapter while igniting a timeless legacy. The Trailanga Swami Math stands proudly, a shrine to his spiritual prowess, inviting all to delve into the mystique of his being.
Explore the sanctum where he meditated, feel the spiritual pulse at Varanasi’s heart. Book a tour with Varanasi Guru and step into the mystical realms Trailanga Swami once roamed – a journey to transcendence, echoing his divine legacy.
Frequently Asked Questions
Why is Trailanga Swami called the “Walking Shiva” of Kashi? Devotees gave Trailanga Swami this title because of his immense yogic powers and his belief that he was a manifestation of Lord Shiva. He was known for miracles such as escaping locked jail cells without a trace, going without food or water for extended periods, and floating on the Ganga, all of which convinced followers he embodied divine, Shiva-like power.
How long did Trailanga Swami live? Trailanga Swami is believed to have lived for 280 years, from 1607 to 1887, which is why he is also remembered as the immortal yogi. He settled in Varanasi in 1737 and spent his final century and a half in the city.
Where can you visit places connected to Trailanga Swami in Varanasi? The Trailanga Swami Math stands near Panchganga Ghat, beside the Alamgir Mosque. It houses a Kali idol he worshipped, a large Shivling he is said to have brought from the Ganga, and the underground meditation chamber where he spent his final years.
How did Trailanga Swami die? Trailanga Swami predicted his own death and directed his disciples to build a wooden box to his exact size. On December 26, 1887, he sat in a yoga posture inside the box, and his disciples carried it by boat from Assi Ghat to be submerged in the Ganga near Panchganga Ghat, without cremation.

documents.title: Traveling To Varanasi: A Guide To Rail, Air, And Road Connectivity
documents.author: Saurabh Rastogi
documents.content:
Varanasi, the cultural and spiritual hub of India, welcomes travelers from around the world with its ancient charm and vibrant energy. As you embark on your journey to this sacred city, understanding the transport hubs is crucial. In this guide, we explore the various railway stations, the airport, and bus terminals in Varanasi, providing essential details on their proximity to the main city, costs, and connectivity with the rest of the country.
Traveling to Varanasi by train
- Varanasi Junction (Varanasi Cantt Railway Station)
Location: Approximately 4 km from the city center
Connectivity: Varanasi Junction, also known as Varanasi Cantt Railway Station, is a major railway hub connecting Varanasi with all major cities across India. Trains ply regularly to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and other significant destinations.
Cost: Train ticket costs vary depending on the class and destination. Varanasi Junction offers a range of services from budget to luxury travel.
Tip: Book your train tickets in advance, especially during peak travel seasons, to secure your preferred class and schedule.
- PT. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction
Location: Approximately 16 km from the Kashi Vishwanath Temple
Connectivity: Mughalsarai Junction is one of the busiest railway stations in the region and a major railway division under East Central Railway. It serves as a crucial junction for trains heading to and from northern, eastern, and central India.
Cost: Similar to Varanasi Junction, ticket costs vary based on class and destination.
- Banaras Railway Station
Location: About 7 km from the city center
Connectivity: Manduadih Railway Station is another important railway station in Varanasi, handling both passenger and freight trains. It is well-connected to major cities like Delhi, Lucknow, and Kolkata.
Cost: Train ticket prices are in line with standard railway fares.
Traveling to Varanasi by air
Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport
Location: About 26 km from the city center
Connectivity: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, also known as Varanasi Airport, has both domestic and limited international flights. It connects Varanasi with major Indian cities like Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata, as well as international destinations like Bangkok and Colombo.
Cost: Flight ticket prices vary based on the airline, class, and destination. Domestic flights are generally more budget-friendly than international ones.
Tip: Check for deals and discounts when booking your flights, and consider flexible travel dates for better fare options.
Travel to Varanasi by bus
- Varanasi Bus Stand (Cantt Bus Station)
Location: Situated around 3 km from the city center
Connectivity: The Cantt Bus Station primarily serves long-distance routes connecting Varanasi with major cities in Uttar Pradesh and neighboring states. Buses ply to destinations such as Allahabad, Lucknow, and Patna.
Cost: Bus fares vary based on the distance traveled and the type of bus. State-run buses are generally more economical than private services.
- Varanasi Bus Stand (Rathyatra Bus Station)
Location: Approximately 4 km from the city center
Connectivity: Rathyatra Bus Station is another major hub catering to both short and long-distance routes. Buses from this station connect Varanasi with nearby towns and cities.
Cost: Similar to the Cantt Bus Station, ticket prices depend on the distance covered and the type of bus service.
Local Transportation in Varanasi
- Auto-rickshaws: Auto-rickshaws, or simply ‘autos,’ are ubiquitous in Varanasi and offer a convenient mode of transport for short distances. Negotiate the fare before starting your journey, and keep in mind that auto-rickshaws are a practical choice for exploring areas such as Ramnagar & Sarnath.
- Cycle Rickshaws: For a more leisurely and eco-friendly option, opt for a cycle rickshaw. These pedal-powered vehicles are a charming way to meander through the narrow alleys of Varanasi, providing a relaxed pace that allows you to absorb the sights, sounds, and aromas of the city. Plus they are allowed to go anywhere in the city where other means of transportation are banned.
- Electric Rickshaws: Varanasi has embraced sustainable transportation with the introduction of electric rickshaws. These battery-operated vehicles offer a quiet and pollution-free mode of travel. Found mainly in crowded market areas and near ghats, these are the perfect choice for exploring specific parts of the city. Hop on for a shared ride!
- Boats on the Ganges: Navigating the Ganges by boat is not only a means of transportation but also an experience in itself. Boat services operate along the river, offering a unique perspective of the ghats and riverside temples. Negotiate prices with boatmen, and consider a sunrise or sunset boat ride for an ethereal view of Varanasi.
- Walking: Perhaps the most immersive way to experience Varanasi is on foot. The labyrinthine alleys and vibrant markets are best explored at a leisurely pace, allowing you to discover hidden gems, street food delights, and the intricate details of the city’s architecture. Walking is not just a means of getting from one point to another but an invitation to absorb the essence of Varanasi.
- Ride Sharing: For a modern and convenient travel experience, Ola, Rapido, and Uber operate in Varanasi. Using their respective apps, you can book cars, auto-rickshaws, and bike taxis. This offers a reliable and standardized option, especially for those who prefer the ease of app-based transportation. (Pro tip: Use the Ola/Rapido app to book bike taxis)
Varanasi’s transportation infrastructure seamlessly blends the traditional and the modern, making it accessible to travelers from various corners of the globe. Whether you choose to arrive by train, plane, or bus, the city’s transport hubs are well-equipped to ensure a smooth and memorable journey. Embrace the diversity of the Indian transportation experience as you navigate the spiritual lanes and cultural wonders of Varanasi.

documents.title: Travelling Solo To Varanasi Like A Local! - Varanasi Guru
documents.content:
A trip to Varanasi is often described as a life-changing experience by many travellers and writers, and it’s no surprise this city has a profound spiritual and cultural aura that leaves a lasting impression. Often, solo travellers are drawn to its unique charm, and many have shared stories of how Varanasi became a turning point in their lives. Whether through its serene ghats, vibrant rituals, or the peaceful energy of the Ganges, Varanasi invites introspection and transformation. It has also served as the backdrop for numerous movies and books, with plot twists often unfolding amidst its ancient streets, temples, and riverside scenes.
If you’ve come across this article, it’s likely that you’ve read about Varanasi, watched a documentary, or been recommended to visit by a friend. Or maybe, just maybe, Varanasi has called to you in ways you cannot explain. Whatever the reason, a solo trip to Varanasi promises to be an unforgettable experience. However, before you embark on this journey, there are a few important things to keep in mind.
Table of Contents
Best time to plan a solo trip to Varanasi
To enjoy the best of Varanasi as a solo traveller, it’s essential to plan your visit during the right season. The months from November to February are ideal, as the weather is pleasantly cold, making it perfect for exploring the ghats and winding streets on foot. During this time, the mornings are misty, the days are comfortable, and the evenings are perfect for experiencing the Ganga Aarti without the discomfort of heat or humidity.
The months from March to June, however, bring intense heat, with daytime temperatures often becoming unbearable, making outdoor activities challenging. If you plan to visit during these months, schedule activities early in the morning or late in the evening to avoid the peak heat.
From July to September, Varanasi experiences the monsoon season. While the rains add a romantic charm to the city, they also bring challenges. Many ghats are submerged due to the rising water levels of the Ganges, limiting access to certain areas. The humidity during this period can also be uncomfortable.
Although Varanasi is a year-round destination, the period between November and February offers the most enjoyable experience for solo travellers, allowing you to make the most of the city’s unique spiritual and cultural offerings.
Where to stay in Varanasi
Since you are travelling solo, it’s highly recommended that you choose the right kind of accommodation for a safe and enjoyable experience. While Varanasi offers all types of accommodations, from luxury hotels to budget stays, it’s crucial to pick one that suits your needs.
No matter which option you choose, ensure that your accommodation is located near the ghats. Avoid booking a stay far from the ghats, as you’ll likely spend a significant amount of time navigating through traffic jams, which can be frustrating. Ideally, your accommodation should not be more than 3 km away from the ghats for convenience.
Once you’ve sorted out the location, the next step is deciding the type of stay. While browsing through numerous booking websites for options is an option, let me save you some time: choose a hostel. Yes, even if you can afford a hotel, hostels are a better choice, and here’s why:
- Lively Atmosphere: Hostels often have vibrant staff and common areas that encourage interaction, making them ideal for solo travelers.
- No Hard-Selling: Unlike some hotels, hostel staff are generally not trying to push commission -based services or tours.
- Community of Travelers: Hostels attract experienced and like-minded travelers, making it easy to connect, share experiences, and even find buddies for city exploration.
- Experienced and Polite Staff: Hostel staff are often knowledgeable and helpful, ensuring you have a smooth and enjoyable stay.
If privacy is a concern, most hostels also offer private rooms, combining the best of both worlds – privacy and a social atmosphere.
My Recommendations: Livefree Hostels, Wanderstation, Moustache Hostel, Safarnama.
Navigating & Going Around
As a solo traveller, especially for women, safety and convenience are paramount. Varanasi’s charm lies in its labyrinthine streets and vibrant ghats, where almost everything is within walking distance. The best part? You’ll rarely feel alone, as the streets and roads are typically bustling with pilgrims, locals, and visible police presence. However, it’s worth noting that after 10 PM, the streets and ghats tend to become deserted, making it ideal to plan your outings accordingly.
Staying close to the ghats has its perks:
- It allows for early morning explorations and nighttime strolls without long commutes.
- You can immerse yourself in the lively atmosphere of Varanasi while being close to the city’s spiritual and cultural pulse.
For those who prefer not to walk long distances, shared e-rickshaws are an economical and easy way to get around. Another fantastic option for solo travellers is motorcycle taxis, which are quick, affordable, and excellent for navigating the narrow streets of Varanasi.
App Recommendations for Bike Taxis:
- Uber
- Ola
- Rapido
These apps provide reliable and efficient services, ensuring you can move around the city comfortably and safely.
Where to eat in Varanasi
Varanasi is a paradise for street food lovers and anyone who enjoys vibrant, flavorful cuisine. Almost every street corner has a popular shop offering something unique, reflecting the city’s rich and diverse food culture influenced by people from all over India. Everything smells and looks so tempting that it’s nearly impossible to resist! However, if you have a sensitive digestive system, it’s important to pace yourself and start slow.
For a safer experience, here are a few tips:
- Begin with hygienic street food shops known for their quality or join a food walk in Varanasi.
- If you’re staying at a hostel, like Livefree, take advantage of their menu. They are known for their amazing food, especially their breakfast offerings, which are both delicious and safe.
Additionally, you can explore some of the cozy and charming cafés around Varanasi that serve a mix of local and international cuisines. This way, you can enjoy the best of the city’s food scene while prioritizing your health.
My Recommendation: Assi ka Dijit Cafe, Pizzeria Vatika Cafe, Filo Cafe, Phulwari Cafe.
Staying safe in Varanasi
I’m keeping this section female-centric because, let’s be honest, women often face more challenges when travelling solo, especially in India. As a local, I want to provide practical, no-nonsense advice tailored specifically for women travellers. For the guys reading this, a quick note: avoid mind-altering substances, steer clear of touts, and don’t hand over money to people selling unsolicited services on the streets. Now, girls, here’s what you need to know for a smooth solo trip to Varanasi:
Essential Tips for Women Travelers
Dress Modestly Opt for attire that covers your shoulders and knees. While Varanasi is generally respectful, modest dressing helps you blend in and avoid unwanted attention.
Avoid Taking Lifts from Strangers Public transport and bike taxis are readily available. Trust licensed services instead of relying on unknown individuals.
Skip the Bhang Lassi if Alone While it’s part of the Varanasi experience, consuming Bhang (a cannabis-infused drink) is best avoided when you’re alone, as its effects can be unpredictable.
Plan Day Trips Wisely If you’re visiting places like Sarnath, leave early around 8-10 AM and aim to return by 4-5 PM to avoid traveling after dark.
Stay Alert but Relaxed Varanasi, being one of India’s holiest cities, is safer compared to many other places worldwide. However, like in any city, remain cautious and aware of your surroundings.
Avoid Traveling During Holi While festivals like Dev Deepawali are spectacular and safe to experience, Holi can be chaotic, with crowded streets and overzealous revellers. It’s better to skip Holi if you’re travelling alone. With these points in mind, your solo trip to Varanasi can be an incredible experience – safe, enriching, and full of memories to cherish.
Booking tours & boat rides
If you’re still hesitant about travelling solo, don’t worry opting for a guided tour can be a perfect starting point. A guided tour not only introduces you to the city’s key attractions but also familiarizes you with its culture, history, and unique ways of life. For first-time visitors to Varanasi, we highly recommend the Subah-e-Banaras Morning Walk.
This walk covers:
- Significant landmarks.
- Historical and cultural insights.
- Practical tips to navigate the city.
Plus, the storyteller can assist you with any questions and provide insider recommendations, making your trip smoother and more enjoyable.
Added Perks:
All of our tours include free text and call assistance throughout your stay in Varanasi. This means you can reach out to us anytime for help or advice, ensuring a stress-free experience.
For boats, it’s best to book boat ride online in advance to avoid any last-minute cancellations or hassles. Additionally, while you can find similar tours from other reputed companies like those on TripAdvisor, booking early ensures availability and a well-planned experience.
With a guided tour, you can ease into the spirit of Varanasi while gaining the confidence to explore the city solo afterwards!

documents.title: Trilochan Ghat - Three Eyed God And Secret Rivers - Varanasi Guru
documents.author: Saurabh Rastogi
documents.content:
Trilochan Ghat is one of the oldest ghats of Varanasi. Kashi Kand marks it as a prominent religious site. In fact, the inscriptions from Gahadavala rule(1100CE) also mention about it. Derived from a temple(Trilochaneshvara) located on this Ghat Trilochan is a Sanskrit word meaning three-eyed Shiv.
Apart from the presence of an ancient temple, Trilochan Ghat has a sacred riverfront which according to Gahadavala inscriptions, was a famous site for sacred bath and rituals. It is also said that the water between the two towers which emerges from the Ganges at this ghat is holy and hold healing powers. According to the local priests, an invisible confluence of Ganges, Narmada, and Pilpippala rivers take place here.
Just like all the sacred sites of Varanasi, this Ghat also faced the fury of Aurangzeb. Trilochaneshvara which was one of the oldest temples of Varanasi was demolished in 1669. It remained deserted for some time until Narayana Dikshit, a powerful priest of Peshwas constructed some stairs in 1740. In 1795 Nathu Bala Peshava reconstructed the temple and built the stairs on entire Ghat. Later on, Govt renovated and built more stairs around the ghat in 1988.
Even after being home to one of the oldest Shivalinga in Varanasi this ghat is not much popular among tourists. Only a few pilgrims and locals take a dip at this ghat.
How to Reach
Trilochan ghat is located near Rabindranath Tagore Road and Gaay Ghat road. It is well connected to all the Railways stations, Airport and the bus stand via road. You can reach here by shared auto-rickshaws which are available from Maidhagin Chowk. One can also take a boat ride from any ghat to the Trilochan ghat.
What to See
- Trilochaneshwar
- Varanasi Devi old image at Trilochaneshwar

documents.title: Tulsi Ghat - House Of Goswami Tulsidas - Varanasi Guru
documents.author: Hrisha Rashmi
documents.content:
Tulsi Ghat- the name itself is self-revelatory, suggesting its associations with the great bhakta poet Tulsidas. It lies in fourth place starting from Assi ghat when moving from south to north along the riverfront Ganga in Varanasi. Earlier, it was a part of an old ghat known as Lolark Ghat. This name became known because of the connection of Goswami Tulsidas with this ghat who wrote Ramacharitmanas. Tulsidas spent the last days of his life living here.
History of Tulsi Ghat
The Hanuman image installed by Tulsidas and a piece of the boat used by him is still preserved in a small temple. The temple is attached to a house owned by Mahant (late) Veer Bhadra Mishra and his family. In 1807 Amrit Rao, the adopted son of Raghoba, made this ghat and also patronized the building, followed by repairs and extensions by Mahant Swami Natha. Later in 1941, Baldeo Das Birla made this ghat pucca. Attached to this ghat is a guesthouse, a Sanskrit School, and the Cleaning Ganga Laboratory – all are under the care of the Sankatmochan Foundation, an NGO founded in 1982. Other than Tulsidas and his belongings, Tulsi ghat has a lot more significance to look up to.
places to visit near Tulsi Ghat:
Tulsidas Ashram: The ashram is located in Tulsi Ghat, precisely where Goswami Tulsidas wrote the classic Ramcharitmanas. The Ashram has an idol of Lord Hanuman installed by Tulsidas himself; a piece of the boat used by him; his khadau(slippers); and his asan(seat).
Lolark Kund: Close to this is a very famous kund, named Lolark Kund. A rectangular water tank of 15m in height. It is one of the oldest sacred places in Varanasi. The structure might date back to around 1000 AD. The word ‘Lolark’ means ‘trembling sun’. The kund displays a wavering image of Sun God, Suryadev, in the water of the tank. Situated on a raised platform immediately south of Lolark Kund, is Sri Lolarkeshwar Mahadev temple or Lolark Aditya Mandir.
Tulsi Akhada: Tulsi or Swaminath Akhada is another nearby place to visit. Here, you’ll see the pehelwans(wrestlers) often performing dand baithaks(sit-ups), jori phirna or wrestling.
Mahishasur Mardini Temple: Also known by the name Chamunda Devi, Mahishasur Mardini is regarded as the Kshetra Rakshika(protector of the region). To the north of Lolark, you can find this temple which also houses the idol of Kaal Bhairav.
Ark Vinayak Temple: This temple offers a rare sight of idols of Vinayak and Vainayaki (feminine form of Ganesh) together. People often misinform tourists that both the idols are of Vinayak facing north and south directions. The pandit of this temple told us about its mention in Kashi Khand (a section of Skanda Mahapuran). It is one of the Ashta Vinayaks located in Kashi. The worship of Ark Vinayak on Guru Poornima has a special significance.
Rani Laxmi Bai Birth Place: At a walking distance from Tulsi Ghat on the way to Assi ghat, stands a grand statue of Laxmibai on the ground of her birthplace.
Festivals to witness near Tulsi Ghat:
Nag Nathaiya: Nag Nathaiya is an important day on the second day of light-half Kartika. It is believed that this Leela was also initiated by Tulsidas himself and is continued till today. A huge branch of Kadamba tree is planted on the Ganga bank and a small boy acting as Krishna jumps from the top of it into the river. Thereafter, he appears standing on the hood of the giant snake (a model) whom he has won the fight under the water. Finally, he puts rope in the snake’s nose and this is followed by his plays on his flute.
Lolark Chatt / Lolark Shashti: It is celebrated in September. Thousands of devotees come here to worship the Sun God. It is noticed that the water of the kund is clear throughout the year, even during the floods. Legends have it that the water here has a special power of fertility and the couples who bathe here are blessed with a child. Also, taking a dip in its holy water cures various skin diseases.
Krishna Leela: During the Hindu lunar month of Kartika (Oct.-Nov.), Krishna Leela (theatrical performance of Lord Krishna’s life) is performed every year at the Tulsi Ghāṭ for almost 15 days.
Ram Leela: Tulsi had also initiated Ram Leela. It takes place for a period of 17 days and ends on the 10th day of the Lunar-Hindu month of Ashvina (Sept-Oct). The first few days of the Leela are performed near the Tulsi Ghāṭ and it finally ends here too. While the rest of the acts are held at different sites in the southern part.
Drupad Festival: It is an annual music festival of 3-4 days held in Tulsi Ghat. Organized in the month of February-March, legendary musicians from around the country come to participate here.
Tulsi Ghat is the next common spot for localities and students after Assi Ghat. You will often witness young musical bands or individuals jamming or practicing here. Jalpari, the river cruise or the queen of Ganga is housed near the Tulsi ghat. You can also see the evening aarti and enjoy riverside Maggi here.
How to reach Tulsi ghat
Tulsi Ghat is located 3KM away from Vishwanath Temple and 2KM away from BHU. It is well connected to all the Railway stations, Airport and the bus stand via road. You can reach Imperial Public School, Assi Road by shared auto-rickshaw, and take a 5-minute walk to the Tulsi Ghat. You can also take a boat ride from any ghat to the Tulsi Ghat or just walk.
Nearby ghats
- Assi ghat
- Rewa ghat
- Bhadaini ghat

documents.title: A Guide To Varanasi International Airport (VNS) - Varanasi Guru
documents.author: Varanasi Guru
documents.content:
Varanasi International Airport or Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ariport is located 24.4KM away from the center of Varanasi. If you’re embarking on an exploration of Banaras by air then it will be your gateway to this mystical land. This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know about your arrival, departure, and airport experience, ensuring a smooth and seamless journey.
Pre-Flight Planning
1. Connectivity: Varanasi Airport is well-connected to major cities in India, with direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Kolkata, and Lucknow. International connections are available, enhancing accessibility for global travelers.
2. Booking: Secure the best deals on flights to VNS by exploring popular booking platforms and airline websites. Compare prices, consider flexible dates, and book well in advance for cost-effective travel.
3. Visas and Immigration: Understand visa requirements based on your nationality, ensuring hassle-free entry into India. Familiarize yourself with immigration procedures and arrival formalities to expedite the process.
Arrival at Varanasi Airport
1. Terminals: Varanasi Airport comprises domestic and international terminals. Domestic travelers can enjoy facilities like lounges, retail outlets, and eateries. International passengers have access to duty-free shopping and other amenities.
2. Baggage Claim: Efficient baggage claim processes and customs procedures are in place for both domestic and international arrivals. Follow signs and guidelines to swiftly retrieve your luggage.
3. Local Currency Exchange: For your convenience, currency exchange services are available within the airport premises and nearby. Consider exchanging currency before venturing into the city.
4. Transportation Options: Various transportation choices await you at the airport, from pre-booked taxis and ride-hailing services to public buses and car rentals. Gain insights into indicative fares and estimated travel times for a seamless journey to Varanasi city. (Try booking via apps such as OLA or Uber for a hassle free experience)
Departure from Varanasi Airport
1. Check-in Counters and Baggage Drop: Locate your airline’s check-in counters and efficiently drop your baggage. Plan your time wisely to avoid the last-minute rush, ensuring a smooth departure process.
2. Airport Amenities: Enjoy a range of amenities within the airport, including restaurants, cafes, shops, duty-free outlets, ATMs, and Wi-Fi connectivity. Make the most of your time before departure.
3. Security and Boarding: Familiarise yourself with security procedures and locate your boarding gate. Ensure you have all the necessary documents for a hassle-free boarding process.
How to Reach the City from Varanasi International Airport (VNS)
Varanasi International Airport is located around 22–25 km from the main city areas like Assi Ghat, Godowlia, Lanka, and Cantt. Here are the best ways to reach Varanasi from the airport.
1. Pre-booked Cab (Most Convenient & Reliable)
The easiest and most comfortable way to travel from the airport to the city is by booking a private cab. You get a clean car, a polite driver, fixed pricing, and a direct drop to your hotel or destination – without waiting or bargaining outside the airport.
Book Your Airport to City Cab
Benefits:
- Timely pickup from the arrival gate
- Clean Sedan or SUV options
- Safe late-night and early-morning service
- Direct drop anywhere in Varanasi
A Glimpse into the Future
Varanasi Airport is poised for a transformative journey with a massive expansion project underway. This initiative includes:
- Runway extension: Extending the runway to 4,075 meters will accommodate larger aircraft and enhance international connectivity.
- New Terminal: A modern and spacious terminal will offer improved passenger facilities and amenities.

- Cargo terminal development: Enhanced cargo handling facilities will boost regional trade and economic activity.
This expansion promises to elevate VNS into a world-class airport, catering to the growing tourist influx and further establishing Varanasi as a premier travel destination.
Additional Information
1. Visa on Arrival: Check eligibility for Visa on Arrival, if available, and follow the prescribed process for a convenient entry into India.
2. Lounge Access: Explore available airport lounges, understanding eligibility criteria and access charges for a relaxing pre-flight experience.
3. Lost and Found: In the unfortunate event of lost items, promptly report to the airport’s lost and found department for assistance.
4. Contact Information: For any queries or assistance, refer to essential contact details for airport authorities, airlines, and other relevant services.
Varanasi Airport (VNS) is dedicated to ensuring passenger comfort and convenience, providing a seamless travel experience. Embrace the wonders of Varanasi and create lasting memories as you embark on a journey into the heart of India’s spirituality and culture. Safe travels!

documents.title: Varanasi Railway Stations: Your Essential Guide
documents.author: Varanasi Guru
documents.content:
Arriving by train unlocks a journey into the ancient land of Varanasi, but navigating its multiple railway stations can be baffling. This comprehensive guide unravels the intricacies of Varanasi’s railway stations, empowering you with crucial information for a smooth arrival.
Varanasi Junction Railway Station (BSB)
Dominating the railway scene, Varanasi Junction, also known as Varanasi Cantt or BSB, stands tall in the heart of the city. Bustling with over 200 trains daily, it connects Kashi to major Indian cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Agra.
Key Features:
- Station Code: BSB
- Platforms: 11 (with one more under construction)
- Amenities: Waiting rooms, retiring rooms, cloakrooms, restaurants, food stalls, ATMs, currency exchange, Wi-Fi, medical facilities, book stalls, and more.
- Connectivity: Extensive network across India, including key pilgrimage sites like Mathura and Haridwar.
- Nearby Attractions: Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple, Assi Ghat, and many more are within easy reach.
Traveler Tips:
- Be prepared for crowds, especially during peak season. Arrive early to ensure a smooth boarding experience.
- Utilize coolie services for luggage assistance at a nominal fee.
- Pre-book train tickets online to avoid last-minute hassles.
- Stay vigilant with your belongings and take necessary precautions against petty theft.
Banaras railway station (BSBS)
Formerly known as Manduadih Station, Banaras Railway Station whispers tales of the past. This heritage station, about 4 kilometers from BSB, offers a tranquil alternative with fewer crowds.
Key Features:
- Station Code: BSB
- Platforms: 6
- Amenities: Waiting rooms, retiring rooms, cloakrooms, restaurants, food stalls, ATMs, Wi-Fi, medical facilities, etc.
- Connectivity: Connects to major cities and pilgrimage destinations like Ayodhya.
- Nearby Attractions: Bharat Mata Temple, Tulsi Manas Temple, and Kashi Vishwanath Temple are accessible.
Traveler Tips:
- Opt for Banaras Railway Station if you prefer a calmer travel experience.
- Pre-book transportation as auto-rickshaws and taxis can be limited.
Kashi Railway Station (KEI)
Offering a contemporary travel experience, Kashi Railway Station (KEI) stands about 6 kilometers east of BSB. Its spacious design and modern amenities make it a popular choice, serving as a secondary station to decongest BSB.
Key Features:
- Station Code: KEI
- Platforms: 3
- Amenities: Waiting rooms, retiring rooms, cloakrooms, restaurants, food stalls, ATMs, Wi-Fi, medical facilities, etc.
- Connectivity: Connects to major cities and pilgrimage sites like Bodh Gaya.
- Nearby Attractions: Sarnath, the renowned Buddhist pilgrimage site, is easily accessible.
Traveler Tips:
- Choose KEI for a modern and comfortable travel environment.
- Be aware that the station is still developing, so certain amenities might be limited.
- Pre-book transportation as public options outside the station can be limited.
Sarnath Railway Station (SCS)
Situated near the renowned Buddhist pilgrimage site of Sarnath, about 13 kilometers from Varanasi Junction.
Key features:
- Station Code: SCS
- Platforms: 2
- Amenities: waiting rooms, restaurants, basic amenities.
- Connectivity: Primarily connects to Varanasi and other major cities in Uttar Pradesh.
- Nearby attractions: Mahabodhi Stupa, Dhamek Stupa, Sarnath Museum.
Traveler Tips:
- Limited facilities
- Pre-book accommodations near Sarnath
- Consider transportation options in advance
Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction (DDU)
Located about 18 kilometers from Varanasi Junction, primarily serving long-distance trains. Often less crowded than other stations.
Key features:
- Station Code: DDU
- Platforms: 5
- Amenities: waiting rooms, retiring rooms, cloakrooms, restaurants, ATMs, Wi-Fi, medical facilities
- Connectivity: Major cities across India, including important pilgrimage destinations like Mathura and Haridwar.
- Nearby attractions: Nothing prominent
- Tips: Check train schedules carefully, and plan transportation as the station is farther from the city center.
With Varanasi Junction, Varanasi Cantt Station, DDU Junction, and Sarnath Railway Station, Varanasi’s railway network ensures diverse connectivity options for travelers. Whether you seek the bustling hub of Varanasi Junction or the historical significance of DDU Junction, each station offers a unique travel experience. Tailor your journey based on destination, preferred routes, and amenities to ensure a seamless and enriching visit to this ancient city.

documents.title: Varanasi Vande Bharat Express: Swift Travel Guide - Varanasi Guru
documents.author: Saurabh Rastogi
documents.content:
Welcome to my comprehensive guide to traveling on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express, one of India’s fastest trains. With its high-speed capabilities and modern amenities, this train offers a seamless journey for passengers. Whether you’re planning a trip to Varanasi or heading to Delhi, the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express is a convenient and efficient mode of transportation.
In this travel guide, we will provide you with all the important details you need to know about the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express. From its route and timings to ticket prices and seat availability, we’ve got you covered.
Introduction to Varanasi Vande Bharat Express
Varanasi Vande Bharat Express is India’s high-speed revolution in railway travel. As one of the country’s fastest trains, it offers a seamless and sophisticated experience for passengers traveling to and from Varanasi. Let’s delve into the significance of this iconic train and explore the amenities that make it a truly remarkable journey.
Route and Timings
The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express, also known as Train number 22436/22435, operates between Varanasi Junction (BSB) and New Delhi Railway Station (NDLS). This high-speed train covers a distance of approximately 800 kilometers, connecting the holy city of Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh with the national capital, New Delhi.
Here are the important details regarding the route and timings of the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express:
Varanasi Vande Bharat Express (Train number 22435):
Departure from New Delhi Railway Station (NDLS): 15:00 PM
Arrival at Varanasi Junction (BSB): 21:55 PM
Varanasi Vande Bharat Express (Train number 22436):
Departure from Varanasi Junction (BSB): 06:35 AM
Arrival at New Delhi Railway Station (NDLS): 02:25 PM
Please note that the timings mentioned above are subject to change. It is advisable to check the official Indian Railways website or contact the railway authorities for the most up-to-date schedule.
Booking Tickets and Fare
Booking tickets is a seamless process. Whether you prefer to book online or offline, there are multiple options available to secure your spot on this high-speed train.
- Online Booking: For tech-savvy travelers, booking tickets online is the most convenient option. Visit the official Indian Railways website or download their mobile app to access the booking platform. Simply enter your travel details, select the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express as your train preference, and proceed with the payment. It’s quick, easy, and offers real-time availability.
- Offline Booking: If you prefer a more traditional approach, you can book tickets for the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express at any of the Indian Railways reservation counters located across the country. Simply visit the nearest railway station, provide your travel details, and the booking agent will assist you in securing your tickets.
Fare Structure
The fare for the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express is based on the distance traveled and the class of accommodation chosen. The train offers both Executive Class and Chair Car seating options.
| Class | Fare Range (INR) | 
|---|---|
| Executive Class | ₹3305 | 
| Chair Car | ₹1750 | 
Please note that the fares mentioned are approximate and may vary based on availability and peak/off-peak season.
Discounts and Offers
- No discounts are available for senior citizens or students on this train.
- Indian Railways occasionally offers promotional discounts and special fares for the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express. Stay updated with their official website or mobile app for any ongoing offers.
Booking your tickets for the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express ensures a comfortable and swift journey through one of India’s most revered cities.
Seating Options in Varanasi Vande Bharat Express
When traveling on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express, you have a range of seating options to choose from, ensuring a comfortable and enjoyable journey. Whether you prefer a cozy seat or a luxurious seat, the train offers something for every traveler’s preference. The Vande Bharat Express between Delhi and Varanasi offers two classes of seating: Executive Chair (EC) and Chair Car (CC).
Executive Chair (EC): This is the premium class, with 52 seats in a 2×2 configuration. The seats are wider and more comfortable than the Chair Car seats, and they recline further. They also have leg rests and headrests. Executive Chair passengers also get access to a personal entertainment system with a touch screen, Wi-Fi, and reading lights.
Chair Car (CC): This is the more budget-friendly option, with 78 seats in a 3×2 configuration. The seats are still comfortable, but they are not as wide or as reclined as the Executive Chair seats. Chair Car passengers do not get access to a personal entertainment system, Wi-Fi, or reading lights.
Here is a table that summarizes the differences between the two classes:
| Feature | Executive Chair (EC) | Chair Car (CC) | 
|---|---|---|
| Seat configuration | 2×2 | 3×2 | 
| Number of seats | 52 | 78 | 
| Seat width | Wider | Narrower | 
| Seat recline | More | Less | 
| Leg rests | Yes | No | 
| Headrests | Yes | No | 
| Personal entertainment system | Yes | No | 
| Wi-Fi | Yes | No | 
| Reading lights | Yes | No | 
Ultimately, the best class for you will depend on your budget and your priorities. If you are looking for the most comfortable and luxurious option, then the Executive Chair is the way to go. However, if you are on a budget or if you don’t mind not having all the bells and whistles, then a Chair Car is a perfectly good option.
Onboard Facilities and Amenities
An unforgettable journey aboard the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express awaits you, complete with top-notch onboard facilities and amenities. Designed with the utmost comfort and convenience in mind, this high-speed train offers an array of services that enhance your travel experience.
- Wi-Fi Connectivity: Stay connected throughout your journey with the train’s complimentary Wi-Fi service. Whether you need to check your emails, browse the internet, or catch up with loved ones, you can enjoy seamless connectivity from the comfort of your seat.
- Food Services: Indulge in a delectable culinary experience onboard the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express. With a variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options available, satisfy your taste buds with dishes prepared by skilled chefs. The spacious dining area ensures a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience.
- Comfortable Seating: Relax and unwind on plush seats designed for maximum comfort. Whether you’re traveling solo or with a group, the train offers different seating arrangements to accommodate your needs. Sit back, relax, and enjoy the scenic views as you journey to your destination.
- Spacious Interiors: Step inside the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express and be greeted by spacious interiors that exude elegance and sophistication. From well-designed cabins to ample legroom, every passenger is provided with a comfortable and luxurious environment throughout the journey.
In addition to the mentioned facilities, the train also offers other amenities to enhance your journey. These include clean and hygienic washrooms, ample storage space for luggage, and attentive staff who are always ready to assist you.
Safety and Security Measures
When it comes to travel, safety and security are of utmost importance. The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express takes these concerns seriously and ensures a secure journey for all passengers. With a range of measures implemented, you can rest assured knowing that every effort has been made to prioritize your well-being.
Here are some of the safety and security features you can expect on board:
- Surveillance Systems: The train is equipped with state-of-the-art surveillance cameras, monitoring the premises at all times. This helps in deterring any potential security threats and ensures a safe environment for passengers.
- Emergency Alerts: In case of any emergency, the train is equipped with alarm systems to immediately notify the onboard staff. Prompt action is taken to address the situation and ensure the safety of all passengers.
- Fire Safety Measures: The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express is equipped with modern fire detection and extinguishing systems. This ensures rapid response and containment in case of any fire-related incidents.
- Security Personnel: Trained security personnel are stationed on board to monitor and maintain a secure environment. They are well-equipped to handle any security concerns and provide assistance whenever required.
These safety and security measures have been implemented to create a worry-free travel experience on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express. The train strives to prioritize the well-being of its passengers and ensure that their journey is not only swift but also secure.
“Passenger safety is our top priority. We have left no stone unturned in implementing the necessary security measures to provide a safe travel experience on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express.” – Railway Official
Entertainment and Connectivity Options
When traveling on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express, you’ll have access to a range of entertainment and connectivity options to make your journey enjoyable and convenient.
- Free Wi-Fi: The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express provides complimentary Wi-Fi access, allowing you to browse the internet, check emails, and stay connected with loved ones.
- USB Charging Ports: Keep your devices powered up with the in-seat USB charging ports, ensuring you never run out of battery.
- Power Outlets: For laptops and other devices that require a power outlet, each seat is equipped with convenient charging options.
With entertainment and connectivity options at your fingertips, your journey on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express will be both entertaining and convenient.
Food and Dining Services
Indulge in a delightful culinary experience aboard the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express. With a range of delectable meals and convenient onboard pantry facilities, satisfy your gastronomic cravings while enjoying your journey.
- Delectable Meals: Experience a diverse menu that caters to a variety of tastes. From mouthwatering regional delicacies to continental favorites, the onboard chefs curate a selection of dishes that will tantalize your taste buds. Whether you prefer vegetarian or non-vegetarian options, there is something to please every palate.
- Onboard Pantry Facilities: Enjoy the convenience of onboard pantry facilities, offering quick bites and refreshing beverages throughout your trip. Quench your thirst with a range of cold drinks, juices, or hot beverages. Treat yourself to snacks and light meals, perfect for satisfying those mid-journey hunger pangs.
“The dining experience on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express is top-notch. The food is delicious, and the staff is attentive and accommodating. It adds an extra touch of luxury to the journey.” – Rajesh Kumar, a frequent traveler.
Whether you’re traveling for leisure or business, the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express ensures that your dining experience is nothing short of exceptional. Sit back, relax, and savor the flavors as you embark on an unforgettable journey.
Tips for a Smooth Journey
Embarking on a journey aboard the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express promises a delightful experience filled with speed, comfort, and convenience. To ensure your trip is truly seamless, here are some helpful tips and tricks:
- Pack Smart: When preparing for your Varanasi Vande Bharat Express journey, pack light to avoid any unnecessary hassle. Carry essential items like toiletries, a change of clothes, and any medication you may need. Additionally, a small bag or backpack for your valuables will keep them secure during your journey.
- Arrive Early: To make the most of your travel experience, arrive at the station well in advance of the scheduled departure time. This will allow you to complete check-in formalities smoothly and find your seat or cabin without any rush. Remember to carry your valid identification documents for verification.
- Familiarize Yourself with the Train Layout: The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express boasts a modern and well-designed layout. Take a moment to familiarize yourself with the train’s different sections, including seating areas, cabins, and amenities. This will help you navigate the train effortlessly and optimize your comfort.
- Follow Travel Etiquette: Traveling in a shared space like the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express requires mutual respect and consideration. Follow basic travel etiquette, such as keeping noise levels to a minimum, refraining from littering, and respecting the personal space of fellow travelers. This ensures a pleasant journey for everyone.
- Stay Connected: Make use of the train’s onboard Wi-Fi to stay connected with friends, family, or work. Whether you want to share your travel moments or catch up on emails, the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express keeps you connected throughout your journey.
- Indulge in the Culinary Delights: The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express offers a delectable range of meals and snacks. Treat yourself to the culinary delights available onboard and savor the flavors of India as you travel to your destination. Don’t miss out on experiencing the diverse cuisine while enjoying the scenic views passing by.
In our opinion, the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express provides an unmatched travel experience, allowing passengers to reach their destination swiftly. However if you are travelling via Chair Car then siting can get a bit tiring and monotonous.
The Varanasi Vande Bharat Express provides a host of amenities and comforts, from comfortable seating arrangements to premium cabin classes, ensuring a pleasant experience for all. The onboard facilities, including Wi-Fi connectivity and food services, cater to the needs of modern travelers.
With a focus on safety and security, passengers can embark on their journey with peace of mind. The train’s implementation of safety measures ensures a secure and worry-free travel experience.
In conclusion, the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express is a remarkable train that combines convenience, speed, and comfort. Whether you’re a leisure traveler or a business professional, this train promises to make your journey an enjoyable one. So, hop aboard and experience the wonders of traveling on the Varanasi Vande Bharat Express!

documents.title: Is Varanasi Wheelchair-Friendly? Accessibility Guide
documents.author: Saurabh Rastogi
documents.content:
A few weeks ago, a family visiting Varanasi with their disabled son reached out to me. They weren’t asking for much, just a wheelchair, an accessible place to stay, temples or ghats with ramps and safe transport around the city. Simple needs. But shockingly, there was barely any reliable information available online to help them.
This moment made me realise how overlooked accessibility still is in a city as spiritual and welcoming as Varanasi. So I decided to put together this guide to help anyone with mobility needs explore this city with dignity, clarity, and joy. Whether you’re planning a trip for yourself, a loved one, or helping someone else, I hope this guide makes things a little easier.
Quick overview: Is Varanasi wheelchair-friendly?
The truth? Varanasi is not fully wheelchair-friendly, especially in the older parts of the city, but that doesn’t mean it’s impossible. With some planning and the right local help, many meaningful parts of the city can be explored comfortably.
- The ghats are mostly stepped, but some, like Gaay Ghat, Assi Ghat and Namo Ghat, are manageable.
- Temples – some modern ones are accessible; others in the old city may require assistance.
- Transport and hotels can be arranged with accessibility in mind.
Wheelchair accessible hotels near Kashi Vishwanath Temple
One of the most important things to do while booking a hotel in Varanasi is to call the property beforehand and confirm its location and accessibility.
Many hotels in Varanasi are situated in narrow, uneven lanes and may not be easily accessible by car or wheelchair. Some buildings have lifts, but not all, so if your room is on a higher floor, it’s crucial to check this in advance.
Also, take a look at the latest Google reviews and user-uploaded photos to get a more accurate idea of the current conditions and amenities.
Pro Tip:
If your only goal is to have darshan at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, then book a hotel close to the temple, ideally on the main road leading to it.
But if you’re planning to stay in Varanasi for a few days, it’s better to stay away from the temple area. That zone is always packed with people, and traffic jams are common. Navigating through it every day can become frustrating and may spoil your overall experience.
Watching the Ganga Aarti with a wheelchair: what’s possible
Ganga Aarti is one of the top attractions in Varanasi, especially the one held at Dashashwamedh Ghat, which is world-famous for its spiritual energy and grandeur.
However, despite its significance, Dashashwamedh Ghat is not wheelchair accessible. The only way to reach the aarti spot is by descending uneven stairs, often wet and crowded, which can be risky and overwhelming.
That said, with a little planning, it’s still possible to experience the magic of the Ganga Aarti. There are locals in Varanasi who are experienced in assisting visitors with wheelchairs. They know the safest routes and will help you reach the aarti spot comfortably.
Contact details for reliable wheelchair assistance are mentioned below.
If you prefer not to hire help but still want to witness the Ganga Aarti, Assi Ghat is a great alternative.
While Assi Ghat is not fully wheelchair accessible, it’s much easier to navigate compared to Dashashwamedh Ghat. There are only 4–5 steps to get down, and after that, the ghat is mostly flat. You can easily park the wheelchair under the large tree near the steps and watch the aarti comfortably from there, with a clear and peaceful view.
Although it’s not the iconic Dashashwamedh Ghat, the ritual at Assi Ghat follows the same process, and the atmosphere is just as spiritual and moving. If you wish to watch the Aarti at Dashaswamedh Ghat, then you can take a boat ride from Gaay Ghat to witness the same.
Wheelchair accessibility at Kashi Vishwanath Temple
The newly built Kashi Vishwanath Corridor is well-planned in terms of accessibility and has been designed keeping senior citizens and differently-abled devotees in mind. The area is spacious, clean, and much easier to navigate than the older temple approach.
Wheelchairs are available from Gate No. 4, located on Gyanvapi/Bansphatak Road. This gate is well-connected by rickshaws and e-rickshaws. If you’re coming from Godowlia, you can also arrange a wheelchair with an assistant for around ₹300-₹400, who will help you get to the temple smoothly.
Inside the temple premises, wheelchairs are available free of cost, provided by the government. The staff and volunteers are generally cooperative and respectful towards accessibility needs.
Wheelchair-friendly boat options in Varanasi
While taking a boat ride in Varanasi is generally safe for senior citizens and differently-abled travellers, the real challenge lies in getting to and into the boat. Most ghats are not wheelchair-friendly, and local boatmen often lack the sensitivity or training to assist those with special mobility needs.
If you’re travelling with a local assistant, you might manage a last-minute booking. But if you’re on your own, preplanning becomes essential to avoid discomfort or unsafe situations.
For those concerned about accessibility, Gaay Ghat is the best place to board. It has fewer stairs, better road connectivity, and flat surfaces that make it easier to reach the boats, even with a wheelchair.
There are also services in Varanasi (including ours) that offer supportive boat rides for seniors and differently-abled guests, with trained staff who understand these needs. Planning ahead can really make all the difference.
Wheelchair-Friendly Places to Explore in Varanasi
While the city of Varanasi wasn’t originally designed with accessibility in mind, there are still several places and temples that can be visited comfortably by senior citizens and differently-abled travellers.
One such place is the Sankat Mochan Temple, one of the most revered temples in the city. It is relatively easy to access and doesn’t involve difficult stairways or narrow lanes.
To make the visit smoother, try going during non-peak hours. The best time depends on the day and local events, so it’s always a good idea to ask your hotel manager for the most suitable time to visit based on your travel dates. Locals usually know the crowd patterns well and can guide you better.
The new corridor area is well-planned for accessibility. With wide, smooth paths and government-provided wheelchairs, visitors can comfortably reach the temple sanctum with some assistance. Use Gate No. 4 (Gyanvapi/Bansphatak Road) for the easiest access.
Assi Ghat is one of the most manageable ghats. There are just 4–5 steps, and the rest is flat ground. It’s a good spot to witness Subah-e-Banaras, Ganga Aarti, or simply relax by the river under the shade of trees.
Namo Ghat is a modern, newly developed ghat with ramps, wider steps, and road-level access, making it one of the best options for wheelchair users. Ideal for boat rides or quiet evenings by the Ganga.
The expansive BHU campus is flat and fully accessible by vehicle. You can visit the iconic New Vishwanath Temple, Bharat Kala Bhawan museum(Ground floor is accessible, there are a few steps at the entry gate), or just drive through the shaded roads. It’s peaceful, clean, and easy to navigate.
Tulsi Manas Temple has manageable entry steps and a quiet environment. Durga Kund is nearby, and while it may need a bit of help at the entrance, the overall layout is easy to move around with assistance.
Sarnath is one of the most accessible sites in the region. The archaeological site, museums, and temples are mostly wheelchair-friendly with paved walkways and ramps. A must-visit for history and Buddhist heritage lovers.
Wheelchair accessible street food shops
While Varanasi is famous for its street food, the narrow, uneven lanes can be tough to navigate in a wheelchair. But that doesn’t mean you have to miss out on the iconic flavours of the city. Here are a few relatively accessible food spots where you can still enjoy the true taste of Kashi.
Kashi Chat Bhandar is fairly popular and located conveniently on the main road near Godowlia. You can try tamatar chaat, aloo tikki, chooda matar, and a hundred other items here to get that real kick of Varanasi street food. In the morning, try the uttapam right near the Godowlia parking, it’s simple, hot, and finger-licking good.
If you’re in the Assi Ghat area, there’s a local vendor who serves soft idlis with chutney in the early morning. It’s a humble setup, but located in a relatively flat and open area that’s easier to access compared to other street food corners.
If you’re looking for a hearty kachodi breakfast, try Golka Kachodi near the Manikarnika Dwar; it’s just 10 meters off the main road and is quite accessible with a wheelchair. Another great option is Neelu Kachodi Bhandar, just about 20 meters from Chowk Thana in the famous Kachodi Gali. Despite being in the old city, this spot is reachable without needing to navigate through too many congested alleys.
Please note: all these places are in different parts of the city, so make sure to check which one is nearest to you before heading out. Asking your hotel staff for help with directions or timing is always a good idea.
Exploring Varanasi with mobility challenges isn’t easy, but with the right information and a bit of planning, it’s absolutely possible. From darshan at Kashi Vishwanath to catching the Ganga Aarti and tasting local flavours, there’s still so much you can experience.
